To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the measured pseudorapidity and transverse momentum dependence of anisotropy flows of charged particles in relativistic heavy ion collisions can be understood by the interplay between string melting and hadronization in the early stage of heavy-ion collisions.

the measured pseudorapidity dependences of v 1 and higher-order anisotropy coefficients of charged hadrons are well reproduced by the string-melting scenario at midrapidity, but the data are better described by the scenario without string-melting at forward pseudorapidities.

the string melting scenario can explain the pseudorapidity- and p T -dependence data of v 2, while the scenario without string-melting can explain better the pseudorapidy- and p T dependence of v 1 and the pseudorapity dependence of v 2.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the string melting mechanism is not necessary for the explanation of anisotropic flow data at forward rapidity, which is consistent with the fact that the string melting scenario has been questioned recently.
the anisotropic flows are sensitive to the formation of partonic matter and to the initial conditions of the collisions.
the pseudorapidity and p T -dependence for the anisotropic flows of charged hadrons are very useful to understand the properties of the hot matter formed in heavy-ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the string melting scenario can explain the measured pseudorapidity and p T dependence of anisotropies in heavy-ion collisions.

the anisotropic flow of hadrons at forward rapidities is a direct probe of the dynamics of string interactions and that the anisotropy of the string interactions can be measured in relativistic heavy ion collisions at the future facility of the high-luminosity large hadron collider.
the pseudorapidity distribution of anisotropic flow is an important observable to probe the early dynamics of relativistic heavy ion collisions.
